core_obligations: Define affine locally finite injective dimension and reduce both cases to X = Spec(A) (proof lines 436-450 and 464-465).
Verify that the two sides commute with the affine comparison functor and that RSheafHom(K, L) has the required boundedness in each case (proof lines 450-460 and 464-468).
Apply the corresponding algebraic evaluation isomorphism (proof lines 460-462 and 468-469).
proof_roadmap: Case (1): definitions, reduction to affine, compatibility and the algebraic statement (proof lines 436-462).
Case (2): the same with the additional coherence input and the technical algebraic statement (proof lines 464-469).
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian scheme X and K, L, M in D_QCoh(O_X), the lemma asserts that the evaluation map RSheafHom(L, M) otimes^L K -> RSheafHom(RSheafHom(K, L), M) of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom-evaluate is an isomorphism in two cases: K in D^-_Coh, L in D^+_Coh and M of affine locally finite injective dimension; and K, L in D_Coh with RSheafHom(L, M) of finite tor dimension and L, M of affine locally finite injective dimension, in particular both bounded (statement lines 414-434). The proof of (1) defines the affine local finiteness of the injective dimension, records in a footnote that the condition is independent of the chosen affine cover, replacing it with an omitted argument, and reduces to X = Spec(A) for a Noetherian ring A (proof lines 436-450). It then observes that RSheafHom(K, L) lies in D^+_Coh by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-coherent-internal-hom and that both sides of the arrow commute with the functor D(A) -> D_QCoh(O_X) by Lemma labelled lemma-affine-duality and Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, after which the arrow is an isomorphism by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism part (2) (proof lines 452-462). The proof of (2) argues the same way but obtains RSheafHom(K, L) in D_Coh affine locally by Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, concluding with More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism-technical (proof lines 464-469). Reducing the sheaf statement to the affine algebraic statement, with both sides compatible with the tilde functor under the stated boundedness hypotheses, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
